brief_item.title: 综述梳理自进化Coding Agent的反馈闭环
brief_item.core_conclusion: 这篇综述把自进化Coding Agent按演化对象、时机和证据来源分类，覆盖记忆、技能工具、模型、框架与工作流。它强调测试、编译错误、CI和代码评审等反馈要进入闭环，但没有提供新的性能测量。
brief_item.mechanism: 分类先区分什么在变，再区分任务时、任务后或阶段式演化，最后标注结果、环境反馈和轨迹信号。软件反馈包括测试、编译器、运行时、仓库历史和评审。
brief_item.result: 综述指出评估不能只看一次pass率，还要覆盖正确性、可维护性、安全、成本、鲁棒性和跨仓库迁移。它把陈旧记忆、噪声反馈、基准过拟合和协作开销列为主要风险。
brief_item.boundary: 这是概念综述，没有统一数据集、效果量、时延、token或成功率；不同系统定义和协议不一致，长期维护性证据有限。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可将项目中的记忆、技能、工具接口和工作流策略分开记录，保存触发变更的证据来源。验收加入Read/Grep/tool-call开销、陈旧记忆失败、成本和跨仓库迁移，不能把综述当作加速实证。

facts.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.03392v1 surveys self-evolving coding-agent taxonomies, evidence, timing, and evaluation risks
facts.problem: Conventional coding agents remain largely static while repositories, dependencies, tests, and project conventions change. Agents may repeat mistakes because they do not retain or transform executable feedback and coding trajectories into reusable behavior, memory, skills, tools, or workflow changes.
facts.mechanism: This survey defines self-evolving coding agents as feedback-driven systems that change future behavior or internal components from software-engineering interactions. It organizes the literature by the object that evolves—agent framework, memory, skills/tools, model, or workflow/topology—and adds orthogonal axes for when evolution occurs (task-time, post-task, stage-wise) and what evidence drives it (outcomes, environmental feedback, trajectories). Software-specific signals include tests, compiler errors, runtime traces, lint/CI results, repository history, patches, and code review feedback.

evidence.claim: The proposed object-centered taxonomy covers evolving agent frameworks, memory, skills and tools, models, and workflow or topology structures.
evidence.condition: Survey classification of representative self-evolving coding-agent work.

evidence.claim: The survey separates evolution timing into task-time, post-task, and stage-wise patterns and evidence into outcome, environmental-feedback, and trajectory-derived signals.
evidence.condition: Orthogonal dimensions used to compare heterogeneous systems.

evidence.claim: Repository-level context and executable feedback are distinctive because coding agents interact with tests, compilers, shells, dependency managers, CI systems, and human reviews, but those signals can be incomplete, noisy, or misleading.
evidence.condition: Conceptual synthesis across the surveyed literature; no new benchmark measurement is reported.

evidence.claim: The survey identifies correctness, maintainability, robustness, cost, safety, benchmark overfitting, feedback reliability, stale memory, and generalization beyond the evolved setting as open evaluation challenges.
evidence.condition: Survey discussion of evaluation and deployment risks for self-evolving systems.
evidence.source_locator: PDF pp.15-17, Evaluation and Open Challenges

facts.evaluation_context: This is a conceptual survey, not a new controlled performance experiment. It reviews coding-agent systems that inspect repositories, invoke tools, execute tests, debug failures, and evolve memory, skills, tools, models, frameworks, or collaboration structures. It argues that evaluation should go beyond one-shot pass/resolve rates to include functional correctness, code quality, safety, efficiency, maintainability, robustness, cost, and transfer to held-out repositories, benchmarks, models, or languages.
facts.limitations: The paper is a guiding synthesis of an emerging area rather than a quantitative meta-analysis; it reports no new common dataset, aggregate effect size, latency, token, or success-rate measurement. Taxonomy categories cover heterogeneous prior systems with different definitions and evaluation protocols. The survey notes risks of benchmark leakage/overfitting, noisy or misleading executable feedback, stale or repository-specific memory, increased coordination cost, and weak evidence for long-term maintainability or cross-domain generalization.
facts.project_relevance: The taxonomy gives a useful design checklist for this project: separate evolving memory/context, procedural skills, tool interfaces, and workflow policy, and record the evidence that triggered each change. It supports measuring not only final task success but also Read/Grep/tool-call overhead, feedback provenance, stale-memory failures, cost, and transfer across repositories; it does not itself prove any acceleration mechanism.
